summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: NAFLD/NASH trials pooled in 38579127 (26 RCTs, favorable lipid, enzyme and steatosis changes, doses not reported) and the Cochrane review of alcoholic/viral liver disease. Dr. Pham's A092 rejects the record's 'liver protection and enzyme normalization' claim and keeps only a narrower NAFLD/NASH reading. The NAFLD meta-analysis (26 RCTs) reports favorable lipid, enzyme and steatosis changes but gives no silymarin dose and mostly tests silymarin added to other active therapy, so it cannot meet the credit rule; the Cochrane review (alcoholic/viral liver disease) found no effect on mortality. The record becomes reference-only, which removes milk thistle Evidence points from dependent products (about 80 per the closure plan).

clinical_review.notes: Signed A092 rejects 'liver protection and enzyme normalization' and keeps only a narrower NAFLD/NASH interpretation. The verified full text does not report silymarin doses and most arms add silymarin to other active therapy, so no credit-bearing NAFLD context can be encoded.

source_provenance.location: Full text via publisher mirror elsevier.es (S1665268123002776): Methods 2.4-2.6, Results 3.1-3.3, Table 1, Discussion limitations.

limitations: Li 2024 (Ann Hepatol; PROSPERO CRD42023398590): 26 RCTs, 2,375 NAFLD/NASH patients; silymarin or silymarin complex versus the same treatment without silymarin, 8-48 weeks (Table 1). Reported SMDs: TC -0.85 (-1.23 to -0.47), TG -0.62 (-1.14 to -0.10, I2 96%), LDL-C -0.81, HDL-C +0.46, ALT -12.39, AST -10.97, fatty liver index -6.64; improved steatosis grade OR 3.25 (1.80-5.87); HOMA-IR SMD -0.37 (-0.77 to 0.04) crosses zero.

No silymarin dose, preparation or dosage form is tabulated in the main text or Table 1; the authors list differing silymarin types and doses as a limitation. Many arms were add-on to lifestyle programs or drugs (statins, pioglitazone, polyene phosphatidylcholine, diisopropylamine dichloroacetate, probiotics); heterogeneity was very high and the ALT/AST 'SMD' magnitudes are implausibly large for standardized differences.
Within signed A092 this is NAFLD/NASH research context only; it does not support general liver protection, enzyme normalization or healthy-aging claims.

clinical_review.notes: Out of scope and null: Cochrane review of alcoholic and hepatitis B/C liver disease with no effect on its primary outcome (mortality). Full text not available (PMC record has no body). Supports no credit for this record.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract (Main results, Authors' conclusions); full text not retrieved.

limitations: Rambaldi 2007 Cochrane review: 18 RCTs, 1,088 patients with alcoholic and/or hepatitis B or C liver disease; milk thistle had no significant effect on mortality (primary; RR 0.78, 0.53-1.15), complications (RR 0.95, 0.83-1.09) or histology; liver-related mortality RR 0.50 (0.29-0.88) in all trials but not in high-quality trials (RR 0.57, 0.28-1.19). Authors question benefit; trial quality low (abstract).
Abstract only; doses and included trials not encoded.
